newsitem.title: INDIA: India defence minister says no Chinese intrusions.
newsitem.headline: India defence minister says no Chinese intrusions.

text.p: Indian Defence Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav on Thursday denied reports of recent Chinese troop infiltrations across the Himalayan border that divides the two countries.
Deputies of the opposition Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) last month alleged in the upper house of parliament that Chinese troops had entered Indian territory.

"In this context I would like to clarify that no intrusions have been made by the Chinese troops in Himachal Pradesh (state), in the middle sector, as referred by some honourable members in the house," Yadav told the upper house.
Himachal Pradesh, one of five Indian states bordering China, is also home to the Dalai Lama, the exiled spiritual leader of Tibet.

"As far as intrusions in the nearby Trig Heights area of the Ladakh region is concerned, I would like to assure the honourable members that the government of India have been observing the situation and are taking the matter up with the Chinese side," he added.
India and China fought a brief border war in 1962. Their relations thawed in 1988 when then-Indian prime minister Rajiv Gandhi visited Beijing for talks with Chinese officials.
The two countries signed a treaty of "peace and tranquility" along their borders in 1993.
India and China also signed an agreement late last year during Chinese President Jiang Zemin's visit to New Delhi to reduce troops and arms along their Himalayan border.
